mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to the previous month's value predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates for equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through stronger corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as higher rates pressure equity valuations.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) relative to the prior quarter predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting immediate market reaction to strong economic growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when GDPC1 expands, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate output and profits.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong labor market and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through elevated consumer spending.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when both PAYEMS and HOUST increase, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 310.0), a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400 units predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as housing activity signals resilient consumer demand despite inflation.
failure_condition: In high-inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 310.0), 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1400, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
